selection_provenance.within_family_ranking: positive development net returns at normal/double costs, >=3 closed and >=1 target; rank lower development cost return
selection_provenance.composition: MU uses breakout-family development winner; SNDK/SKHYNIX use transition-family development winners

notes: Each stock has its own capital, ledger, risk budget and profit assessment; other stocks cannot offset a failed individual acceptance check.
Fixed equal capital buckets; no redistribution of profits or losses across stocks.
At most one position per bucket, at most three overall; each trade risks 0.5% of its own bucket, approximately 0.167% of starting total capital.
All three use the same fee/funding/mark/stop/target execution model and uniform five-minute history. No single-trade classification overrides.
Initial margin target remains net 120% at isolated 10x; no averaging down, martingale or extra leverage.
Historical family composition is research development and may overfit; a future paper period is needed before live qualification.
Rules frozen before replay; no parameter sweep or winner selection.
Only completed candles are visible; earliest entry is next 4h opening.
Net target uses initial isolated margin and actual accumulated funding, not account equity.
Both directions use symmetric trend/breakout rules; no averaging down or pyramiding.
Conservative one-hour stop-first execution; exact intrabar order, historical order book, historical margin tiers and event-calendar coverage are unavailable.
Current fee and maintenance assumptions require venue confirmation before execution; this candidate cannot submit live orders.
Use conservative 0.10% taker fee per side uniformly; current Aster fee documentation classifies SKHYNIX separately from the lower RWA fee group.
Current public Aster tier for notional below 1,000,000 USDT has 1.5% maintenance margin and permits up to 50x; historical tier changes are unavailable. Stress at 5% maintenance margin.
Evaluation is retrospective chronological replay, not a new unseen or forward-tested sample.

liquidity_experiment.hypothesis: Use prior completed five-minute volume to cap quantity; reject unavailable or zero volume. No signal-date exclusions, current-bar final-volume lookahead or parameter grid.
liquidity_experiment.warning: A proxy for admission and sizing, not proof of opening-tick order book depth, actual fills or subsequent stop liquidity.

coverage_choice.method: Discard execution AND indicator history through the last unavailable bar, aligned to next 4h boundary. Rewarm all signals on the remaining actual history; do not interpolate.
coverage_choice.warning: Full means the complete remaining suffix, not each symbol's listing-to-date history. Earlier trades and indicator warmup are excluded.

limitations: Fixed selected profiles; no additional parameter optimization. All history has been inspected and is retrospective.
Recent windows start flat, with prior causal indicator warmup; monthly contributions use continuous full-history inventory and are mark-to-market, not realized PnL.
Trade/mark five-minute paths still leave unknown intrabar order and assume stop execution; liquidation-first when both cross inside the same bar.
Current rules, assumed fees/slippage and approximate funding settlement marks cannot establish historical executable fills.
Stress sizing responds to changed costs; slippage stress is a uniform fill assumption, not measured depth or a delayed-stop simulation.
Each symbol's capital stays separate. End-close is an estimate and net120 counts include closed trades only.
Historical block resampling is descriptive of the selected finite sample and omits uncertainty from candidate selection.
